analyzed_vuln.description: `get_coffset` calls `blosc_getitem(coffsets, nchunk, 1, offset)` on attacker-controlled `coffsets` data returned by `get_coffsets`, but `blosc_getitem` is invoked with `srcsize=INT32_MAX` and therefore does not have a real bound for the compressed buffer. With malformed frame offset-chunk data, `_blosc_getitem`/`blosc_d` trust bogus block offsets and `sw32_` dereferences an invalid pointer, causing the SEGV. Crash manifests in `sw32_` (`blosc-private.h:90`) during this decompression path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In `decompress_frame_fuzzer`, input bytes are parsed as an in-memory frame (`blosc2_schunk_from_buffer`). During chunk decompression (`frame_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_get_lazychunk` -> `get_coffset`), the frame’s compressed offsets chunk must be malformed so that decoding it via `blosc_getitem` reads invalid block metadata/offsets. Because no true source-length is passed to `blosc_getitem`, crafted offsets data can drive out-of-bounds reads and crash in `sw32_`.
